ănădēmă , ătis, n., = ἀνάδημα,
I.a band, a fillet, an ornament for the head: Et bene parta patrum flunt anademata, mitrae, the well-earned property of fathers is converted into head-bands, etc., * Lucr. 4, 1129; Dig. 34, 2, 27.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
